messages.subject: Amplitude filtering before ACI calculation of multiple files
messages.subject_clean: Amplitude filtering before ACI calculation of multiple files
messages.body_plain:
I need to calculate Acoustic Complexity Index (ACI) of hundreds of .wav files as part of a Soundscape Ecology study.

The soundecology package in R has a very useful function multiple_sounds () function. However, I couldn't find any amplitude filter in the package.

seewave package has afilter () which allows to set filtering of amplitude by setting at certain thresholds.

I would like to use afilter () to many .wav files in a folder and then to apply multiple_sounds () to all the filtered files. Since I am new to R, I am at a loss to combine or loop these two functions to get desired results.

Can you please help me in this?

Examples:

afilter (.wav files,f=22050,threshold= 5,plot= F)

multiple_sounds (directory = "C:/Users/pc1/Desktop/sound",
            resultfile = "C:/Users/pc1/Desktop/sound/results1.csv",
            soundindex = "acoustic_complexity",min_freq = 1500, max_freq =
            12000, j = 5, fft_w = 512)

Thank you,

Ana

messages.subject: problems with resample
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
    I'm using resamp() to resample files recorded at very high sample rates but with useful content only in the lower part of the bandwidth. If a resamp() a stereo file I get these two problems
1 - I get resampled only the Left channel, in the output the Right channel is set to null, and the stereo flag is set to false.
2 - the rsult I get even from a 24 bit wav file is a 16 bit signal

Here my code and the rsults I get:
soundfile=readWave(filename,0,1,units="minutes")    # here I read one minute of a stereo wav file with 24 bit data
soundfileresampled=resamp(soundfile,f=312500,g=102400,output="Wave")

soundfile

Wave Object
Number of Samples:      18750000
Duration (seconds):     60
Samplingrate (Hertz):   312500
Channels (Mono/Stereo): Stereo
PCM (integer format):   TRUE
Bit (8/16/24/32/64):    24

soundfileresampled

Wave Object
Number of Samples:      6144000
Duration (seconds):     60
Samplingrate (Hertz):   102400
Channels (Mono/Stereo): Mono
PCM (integer format):   TRUE
Bit (8/16/24/32/64):    16

How I can force to maintain stereo and bit depth of the original file ?

second point: which type of filtering is performed before/after resampling ?

Gianni Pavan

PeakResampled                                                           # peak level is the same as above - that is strange

Gianni

messages.body_plain:
Hi Ana,

I am also an R novice, so bear with me, but perhaps you could just use a for loop?
There are surely more efficient ways to process through a directory...

I think the key is to get each .wav file recognized, then seewave (or soundscape) can work.
For example,

library(tuneR)
library(seewave)
#create an empty space for results to be stored
result=NULL
output=NULL
# create directory
l<-list.files("/yourdirectory",full.names = T)
# write a for loop to sequence through directory for the total number of files in directory
for (i in length(l)){
  #read each file, as a single object
  y1<-i
  y2<-readWave(y1)
  y3<-afilter(y2,f=22050,threshold= 5,plot= F)
  # then write file, or do whatever is next
  # result=ACI(y3)
  # output<-rbind(result,output)
  }

I hope this is helpful.

Adam

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Re: Amplitude filtering before ACI calculation of multiple files
messages.subject_clean: [seewave] Re: Amplitude filtering before ACI calculation of multiple files
messages.body_plain:
I think you can simplify the code a bit if you use the package "purrr" (yes, with three Rs), avoiding the for(). The map function is a bit like a simplified apply(), as in it applies the desired function to a given list.

The code can be further streamlined by using pipes, but I think way is easier for novices to understand what is happening in each line (and to debug any errors). It may require a lot of memory if the files are big, as it reads all files before calculating the index, in which case the for() solution may be a better option, as files are read one by one

library(purrr) # map() function
library(seewave) # ACI() function

files<-list.files()
waves <- map(files, readWave)  # reads all files in directory into a list
filtered <- map(waves, afilter, f=22050,threshold= 5,plot= F, output="Wave") # filters files read in line above, returning a list
ACIS <- map_dbl(filtered, ACI) # calculates ACI for each filtered sound, returning a vector of values

Cheers,
 Vitor

messages.subject: zoom in on a spectro plot in both time and amplitude?
messages.subject_clean: zoom in on a spectro plot in both time and amplitude?
messages.body_plain:
I'm a total novice on seewave - tried to solve this on my own for a couple of days.

I am displaying a wave file in a plot, I want to "zoom in" on the plot to display the part of interest (in this case, a bird call).  I've learned how to read in part of the wave file by a range of time, effectively zooming in on the time axis.  How can I zoom in on the aplitude axis, such that I display only from, say 0 to 3 kHz in this example?  what if I only wanted to display something in the middle (e.g., in this example, 3-4 kHz)?

# ----------------
# grabbing file off of online repository:
url <- "http://www.xeno-canto.org/13605/download"
file <- "113605.mp3"
download.file(url, destfile=file, quiet=TRUE)
flammulated_owl <- readMP3(file)

# convert to wave file
savewav(flammulated_owl, f=44100, filename = "flammulated_owl_conv.wav", rescale=c(-1500,1500)) #convert the mp3 to wav

#read in the .wav file created from .mp3
flamowl <- readWave("flammulated_owl_conv.wav")
# crop time to the first 1 second, to zoom in on call
flamowl_crop <- readWave("flammulated_owl_conv.wav", from=0, to=1, units="seconds")

spectro(flamowl, osc=TRUE) # original file
spectro(flamowl_crop, osc=TRUE) # cropped in time to 0-1 second
#------------

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] zoom in on a spectro plot in both time and amplitude?
messages.subject_clean: [seewave] zoom in on a spectro plot in both time and amplitude?
messages.body_plain:
You can use the parameter flim to determine which part of the spectrogram will be plotted on the frequency axis (in kHz), and tlim will do the same for the time axis (in seconds). Both parameters take a two element vector as in c(start, finish)

spectro(flamowl, osc=TRUE, flim = c(0,3))

Cheers,
Vitor

messages.subject: tuneR: Problems with reading in wave
messages.subject_clean: tuneR: Problems with reading in wave
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Recently, I have been trying to find the optimal automatic USV detection and classification from mice. Therefore, I am trying out different software and their scripts. However, I am quite keen on R, nonetheless, still a beginning coder. Consequently, I wanted to run a script recently created by Xiaoling Dou in R for the aforementioned purpose, however, I ran into some issues.

Article and DOI Xiaoling Dou (2018):
https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0196834
Doi: 10.1371/journal.pone.0196834

My question is twofold:

My first problem starts with readWave function of the tuneR package, namely, every time I want to read in a .WAV file from the lab where I am currently doing an internship it gives me the following error: "Error in readWave("3C.wav") : No data chunk found". Furthermore, peculiar enough I do not get this error when I read in .WAV files obtained through opensource data and so on.

Secondly, I have to perform a discrete fourier transform afterwards for which I would like to specify certain characteristics such as frame duration, frame overlap, squared amplitudes and so on following the article written by Xiaoling Dou (2018).

Finally, I do realise that this post is not specifically about "seewave", nonetheless, since tuneR and seewave complement each other, I hope someone can help me out with my first and biggest problem. Also, I tried “load.wave” from the “audio” package (where I can load in the files), however the vector given is too long for larger .WAV files (couple of minutes) and there is no function to specify the range as in readWave (x, from =, to =), which I would really like to utilize.

Thank you in advance!

Kind regards,

Bavo

It could be that the lab's files are incorrectly formatted. Here are two things you can try.

1. Play the waves files in a sound player, even if they're not supposed to be sounds, and check what the encoding is or what error messages are produced.
2. Compare the lab files to wave files of the same encoding. You can open them in R with readBin.
